intro: The Central African Republic lies at the heart of Africa. Rich in diamonds and forests, it has suffered years of coups and conflict.

chapters.title: Early peoples
text: Megaliths at Bouar are thousands of years old. Many peoples, including the Banda, Gbaya and Aka forest people, lived here. In the 1800s raids for enslaved people devastated the region.

chapters.title: Oubangui-Chari
text: France ruled it as Oubangui-Chari from the 1890s, and private companies forced people to collect rubber. It became independent in 1960.

chapters.title: Coups and conflict
text: Jean-Bédel Bokassa crowned himself emperor in 1977 in a lavish ceremony before being overthrown in 1979. Since 2013 fighting between armed groups has displaced over a million people. Russian forces now support the government.
